entries.title: Japan: Strong earthquake hits Kumamoto, several dead
entries.snippet: Dozens of people were hospitalized after the earthquake hit southern Japan. According to media reports, at least two women were killed after a shopping mall partially collapsed in the town of Kashima.

entries.title: Iran war: Netanyahu hails closed-door meeting with Trump
entries.snippet: The meeting between the US President and the Israeli Prime Minister is the first since the start of the war in Iran. Meanwhile, Tehran executed two men for their role in anti-government protests.

entries.title: Zelenskyy visits Trump as Ukraine seeks stronger air defense
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is seeking stronger military cooperation, as Kyiv and Moscow intensify long-range strikes amid stalled peace efforts.

entries.title: UN says online scam center trafficking is skyrocketing
entries.snippet: Migration authorities have said gangs are trafficking ever more people to East Asian online scam centers. The UN says some 300,000 people from more than 80 countries are currently being exploited and abused.

entries.title: Guyana: Captain, crew charged with murder in ferry capsizing
entries.snippet: Police in Guyana have charged three men with murder in connection to a recent ferry capsizing that killed 73 and left 30 missing. Some lawmakers, however, blame government officials for the deadly accident.

entries.title: Fujimori takes charge in Peru amid China, US balancing act
entries.snippet: Peru's new president, Keiko Fujimori, has promised more security and investment. Now in office, she'll have to find space for the South American nation amid Washington and Beijing's geopolitical rivalry.

entries.title: FIFA plans to form new commercial subsidiary and sell stake
entries.snippet: FIFA has announced plans to form a commercial subsidiary and to sell a non-controlling interest to private investors. It needs approval from member associations, but is claiming that it will benefit them financially.

entries.title: Germany: Low Rhine River levels could push economy into stagnation
entries.snippet: Record-low water levels on the Rhine are forcing cargo vessels to run with sharply reduced loads, driving up transport costs. Economists warn the disruption could wipe out Germany's already weak summer growth.

entries.title: Fact check: Berlin Pride attack claims debunked
entries.snippet: Following the Islamist terrorist attack at Berlin Pride, rumors, false claims and misleading videos have been spreading on social media. DW Fact check examines some of the most widely shared claims.

entries.title: EU civil protection mechanism: Coordinating Europe's firefighters
entries.snippet: French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has become increasingly effective, yet it will reach its limits in the summer of 2026.

entries.title: Poland: Top court rejects recognizing EU same-sex marriages
entries.snippet: Poland's constitutional court has overturned plans to recognize same-sex marriages that took place in other EU member states. This defies an order from the EU's top court and could set up a clash on the matter.

entries.title: Could US airstrikes stop insurgency in Mali?
entries.snippet: US President Donald Trump is considering airstrikes against the Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM in Mali, according to multiple reports. Analysts say such attacks might weaken the jihadists but would not address the core issues.

entries.title: Why is Germany building roads for yesterday's climate?
entries.snippet: As the Autobahn buckles under heat waves, Germany is still paving roads for a past climate. Engineers know how to fix that — so what's the holdup?

entries.title: Will Pakistan intervene amid Houthi attacks on Saudi ships?
entries.snippet: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are strategic defense partners, but experts say there are limits to how far Islamabad can go in opposing Iran-backed Houthis.

entries.title: Germany: Online tourist accommodation bookings hit new peak
entries.snippet: Vacation rental bookings through online platforms have climbed to a new record in Germany. The figures reveal major regional differences in where certain tourists like to go.

entries.title: 'Loneliness influencers': Being alone brings in the clicks
entries.snippet: No friends, no dating, no problem? Many influencers are presenting social isolation as a lifestyle. But experts warn of the consequences.

entries.title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern and WAFCON

entries.title: As US-Iran war rages, who's risking the Strait of Hormuz?

entries.title: Germany news: IS video found on Berlin Pride suspect's phone
entries.snippet: Berlin Pride suspect Abdul B. pledged allegiance to the "Islamic State" in a video filmed prior to the attack. Meanwhile, Germany's center-left wants constitutional protections for LGBTQ+. DW has more.
